msItem.title: Amores 3.8

handDesc.handNote: Main text and any darker interventions are distinguished where observed. No individual historical correcting hands are inferred from tonal contrast in monochrome photographs.

origin.p: The supplied BnF IIIF manifest dates the manuscript to 1001–1100. The catalogue dating is not a date assigned to individual interventions.

surrogates.p: The original full-resolution digital images and enlarged crops were inspected for this first pass. Gallica source reuse conditions apply. No text was populated from LL or another witness.

projectDesc.p: Source-grounded first reading of all 66 annotated verse positions, with manuscript-specific spellings and observed interventions. Independent second reading is required before integration as reviewed.

correction.p: No silent emendation from an edition or another witness. Local uncertain letters use unclear, irrecoverable text or signs use gap. Observed above-line letters use add. Tonal distinctions use hi without an invented underlying erased text or historical hand. Manuscript annotations use note type manuscript, distinct from editorial evidence notes.

normalization.p: One source-oriented display. Ordinary allographs, long s, and capitals are represented in legible Latin types. Word boundaries are editorially segmented; no indentation whitespace is inserted inside verse mixed content. Selected ligatures and abbreviation signs are declared typographic approximations; explicit expansions remain in TEI rather than a separate reading mode. This is not a facsimile-perfect inventory of every minute stroke.

punctuation.p: Significant observed punctuation is retained schematically, without adding systematic modern sentence punctuation.

segmentation.p: Each l represents a verse and physical written line at its canonical poem position. Elegiac couplets and even-line indentation are editorial display grouping. Page breaks follow the photographed left/right physical pages. Facsimile zones reproduce the existing annotation rectangles unchanged; they may include neighbouring ink and exclude marginal annotations.

interpretation.p: First-pass evidence notes are a working queue for an independent agent, not assignments for the human editor. Genuine source uncertainty remains local; consequential unresolved interpretation is distinguished from ordinary observation.

revisionDesc.change: Completed first reading from source images and enlarged crops, with line coverage and evidence notes. Independent second reading not yet performed.

div.head: First-pass evidence notes
div.note: A large E extends beside the initial couplet. The three-line marginal heading is faded; only AD, tentative EAM, and tentative IS EST are retained. The unreadable heading is not reconstructed from an edition. Unclear source traces retained: EAM; IS EST. Gap elements represent unreadable text in an inspected extant position, not manuscript absence. No text is filled from LL or another witness.
Unclear source traces retained: tenerum.
Pulchre domine is retained as the manuscript spelling.
Unclear source traces retained: Turpiter.
Image 93 left begins this verse; the first phrase is faint. Unclear source traces retained: Ecce recens.
Qua periit aliquis is the apparent source reading; it is not silently normalized.
The spelling pugne is retained.
The men portion of carmen is darker than surrounding letters. It is represented as tonal difference, without an invented earlier reading or hand. A terminal point is preserved.
Unclear source traces retained: pilum.
The apparent spelling ammonitus is preserved, rather than regularizing it to admonitus.
The initial phrase looks like Erati postes but is faint. The transcription does not insert an unattested initial vowel without source support. Unclear source traces retained: Erati postes.
Unclear source traces retained: sapiens in munere.
Celi saturnus is the apparent spelling and order. No normalized caelum or name capital is inserted.
This final line on image 93 left is faded. The complete phrase is tentative and requires fresh source scrutiny. Unclear source traces retained: Omne lucrum tenebris alta premebat humus.

Image 93 right begins here; the last word is too dark or faded to establish securely. Gap elements represent unreadable text in an inspected extant position, not manuscript absence. No text is filled from LL or another witness.
Nulla que is segmented as visible words; no reconstructed morphology is imposed.
Absque is tentative in the faint middle of the line. Unclear source traces retained: absque.
The adjective before remo is tentatively eruta; it is not corrected to a familiar line. Unclear source traces retained: eruta.
A dark patch reaches the end of the verse; fuisses remains legible.
The final name is obscured by dark marking or surface disturbance; quirinus is a tentative reading, not proof of an original final ending. Unclear source traces retained: quirinus.
The opening Liber et alcides is faint and tentative. The distinct following et ligature is expanded in TEI. Unclear source traces retained: Liber et alcides.
The opening is faint; Curia pauperibus is tentative. Clausa est dat census honores is more legible. Unclear source traces retained: Curia pauperibus.
Unclear source traces retained: Inde grauis iudex inde seuerus eques.
A dark stain crosses the final word forumque. The proposed reading remains unclear. Unclear source traces retained: forumque.
The opening is faded, with Seruiat hi pacem retained tentatively. Unclear source traces retained: Seruiat hi pacem.

The lower part of image 93 right is severely faded with localized dark marks. Only partial traces are retained; the rest of the extant verse is a legibility gap. Unclear source traces retained: auidi; amoris. Gap elements represent unreadable text in an inspected extant position, not manuscript absence. No text is filled from LL or another witness.

No complete source reading is secured for this faded physical line; only tentative pauperis is retained. Unclear source traces retained: pauperis. Gap elements represent unreadable text in an inspected extant position, not manuscript absence. No text is filled from LL or another witness.

Only tentative ille can be separated securely enough to retain; other text remains gaps. Unclear source traces retained: ille. Gap elements represent unreadable text in an inspected extant position, not manuscript absence. No text is filled from LL or another witness.

Only tentative multa is retained amid gaps; no familiar sentence has supplied the rest. Unclear source traces retained: multa. Gap elements represent unreadable text in an inspected extant position, not manuscript absence. No text is filled from LL or another witness.

Tentative custos and maritum surround partly illegible text; illa is clearer. Unclear source traces retained: custos; maritum. Gap elements represent unreadable text in an inspected extant position, not manuscript absence. No text is filled from LL or another witness.

Tentative cede and final domo survive. The rest is too faint to complete. Unclear source traces retained: cede. Gap elements represent unreadable text in an inspected extant position, not manuscript absence. No text is filled from LL or another witness.

Image 94 left begins with the final couplet, followed immediately by the large initial of P 3.9. The beginning and ending of this verse remain tentative. Unclear source traces retained: Si modo quisquam; amantes.
Puluere mutet is a tentative first-pass segmentation of faded continuous letters. No preposition or ending has been supplied from another witness. Unclear source traces retained: puluere mutet.
